analysis.title: Capri Holdings (CPRI): F2Q27 First Take: Better-than-expected 2Q results; FY27 outlook raised
key_insights: CPRI reported F2Q27 adjusted EPS of $0.42 vs GS/FactSet consensus of $0.21. GAAP EPS was $0.25 after $0.17 of one-time items.

Net sales fell 5.5% Y/Y (-4.9% ex-FX) to $809mn vs GS/consensus of -9.0%/-8.1%. After adjusting for a ~$20mn wholesale shipment timing shift, sales fell 7.8% vs consensus -8.1%, so the beat was more modest.

Jimmy Choo sales rose 11.5% Y/Y (+7.6% adjusting for timing) to $146mn vs GS/consensus +2.9%/+3.1%. Michael Kors sales fell 8.6% Y/Y (-10.6% adjusting for timing) to $663mn vs GS/consensus -11.1%/-10.9%.
Gross margin was 63.3%, up ~230bps Y/Y, above consensus of 63.0% but below GSe of 64.0%. Drivers were higher full-price sell-throughs, brand mix and lower tariff rates Y/Y.
Adjusted EBIT margin was 3.8% vs GS/consensus of 1.4%. EBIT was $31mn vs GSe $10.6mn. SG&A was $481mn, 59.5% of sales, vs GSe 62.6%.
Segment margins: Michael Kors 10.3% vs GSe 8.9% (~20bps Y/Y expansion). Jimmy Choo 1.4% vs GSe -5.4% (~830bps Y/Y improvement, driven by expense leverage on higher revenue).

FY27 guidance raised: adj. EPS ~$2.20 (from $2.15) vs GS/consensus $2.13/$2.11. Revenue ~$3.420bn (from ~$3.4bn) vs GS/consensus $3.396bn/$3.401bn. Adj. operating income ~$175mn (from ~$170mn) vs $165.7mn/$167.4mn.

Brand revenue guidance for FY27: Michael Kors ~$2.770bn (from ~$2.765bn), Jimmy Choo ~$650mn (from ~$635mn). Segment margin forecasts are unchanged at low double digits for MK and low single digits for JC.
FY guidance assumes an incremental 10% tariff rate through July 24, 2026 and 10%-12.5% thereafter.

3Q guide: adj. EPS ~$0.95 vs GS/consensus $0.94/$0.93. Sales ~$1.005bn vs $1.012bn/$1.019bn, reflecting ~$20mn of wholesale shipments pulled from 3Q into 2Q. MK revenue ~$830mn vs consensus $844mn, JC ~$175mn vs $175mn, operating income ~$90mn vs GS/consensus $108.3mn/$109.6mn.
Management said trends improved each month of the quarter. GS is encouraged by the sequential strength and by the flow-through of the 2Q profit beat to a higher full-year operating profit guide.
GS is Neutral with a 12-month price target of $18 (6.25x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA), 12.1% above the $16.06 price as of the 10/29 close. Market cap is $1.8bn.

Questions for the call: Michael Kors trends by geography and channel and confidence in the guided second-half acceleration, drivers of sequential improvement, sustainability of Jimmy Choo growth and profit, portfolio thoughts, and second-half margin puts and takes including the wholesale timing impact.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and the $18 target after the F2Q27 beat and raised FY27 guide. The 3Q operating income guide is below consensus and part of the beat came from wholesale shipment timing.

risk_factors: Upside risks: faster sales recovery and growth, faster margin recapture from improving brand heat, stronger cash flow generation.
Downside risks: longer path to sales improvement, sustained margin compression, balance sheet and FCF deterioration.
Part of the 2Q outperformance came from earlier wholesale shipments (~$20mn), which reduces 3Q sales and operating profit.
Tariff assumption risk: guidance assumes an incremental 10% tariff rate through July 24, 2026 and 10%-12.5% thereafter.

tension_points.bull_case: Adj. EPS of $0.42 beat the $0.21 consensus, both brands' sales guides were raised, trends improved each month of the quarter, and the stronger 2Q operating profit flowed through to a higher FY operating income guide of ~$175mn.
tension_points.bear_case: Part of the beat came from ~$20mn of wholesale shipments pulled forward from 3Q. After adjusting, the sales beat was modest (-7.8% vs consensus -8.1%). 3Q sales (~$1.005bn) and operating income (~$90mn) are guided below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A failure to deliver the guided second-half sales acceleration at Michael Kors, which is the first item GS wants addressed on the call.

theme_stances.key_argument: GS is encouraged by management's commentary on sequential strength, a raised sales guide for both brands and flow-through of the 2Q profit beat to a higher full-year operating profit guide.
theme_stances.evidence: we are encouraged by management's commentary regarding sequential strength in trends
